newsitem.title: USA: Poll shows U.S. entertainment tops in world.
newsitem.headline: Poll shows U.S. entertainment tops in world.

text.p: Most consumers around the world give U.S. entertainment the highest rating of any country, according to a poll released Tuesday, although Britain and France view American content as inferior to their own.
In an international poll done by the Gallup organization for the New York-based Bozell advertising agency, 41.5 percent of international consumers rate U.S. entertainment "excellent" or "very good."
That was twice as high as the country with the next-highest approval, Britain, ranked highly by 20.5 percent of consumers.

The Bozell-Gallup poll asked 20,000 consumers in 19 countries to give their opinions of products from different countries. The annual survey, which in the past has ranked only manufactured goods, for the first time included entertainment products like movies, television programs and sports.

It found widespread acceptance of American content, even in countries where domestic entertainment is admired, like Japan, which gives its own products a 57 percent rating and those from the United States a 76 percent. Chinese consumers heavily favored U.S. entertainment, with 47 percent rating it highly favorably vs. 16 percent for home-grown entertainment.

In France, where officials who have fought the "Americanization" of film and television, only 23 percent of consumers gave U.S. entertainment a very positive rating, compared with 27 percent for domestic content.
Britain's consumers preferred local talent by an even wider margin, with 64 percent viewing British entertainment as superior and only 46 percent rating American products very good or excellent.

The poll showed Japanese entertainment products ranked No. 3 worldwide after the United States and Britain. Helped by its ubiquitous video games, it scored highly with 19.8 percent of global consumers. Germany (16.9 percent) edged out France (16.1 percent) as No. 4. Italy was No.6.

On the manufacturing side, Japan held its ranking as the worldwide consumer favorite for the third year in a row, followed by Germany and the United States. Japan was ranked favorably by 41.5 percent; Germany was 35.1 percent.

The perception of U.S. manufactured goods internationally rose to 34.9 percent from 32.2 percent the prior year. But American manufacturers slipped in one important category: American consumers now rank Japanese goods above domestic goods, by a 49-46 margin.

"Our study documents the extent to which the U.S. entertainment industry has won over people everywhere from China to Chile,"said Charles Peebler, chief executive of Bozell, Jacobs, Kenyon & Eckhardt."But it also shows countries which are more resistant to "Americanization," where the marketplace for entertainment is quite competitive."

The survey reached about 1,000 consumers in each of 19 countries, including, Canada, Chile, China, Columbia, Domincan Republic, France, Germany, Hungary, India, Japan, Lithuania, Mexico, Singapore, Spain, Taiwan, Thailand, Great Britain, the United States and Venezuela.
